style: Same dark-gold editorial system as sibling pieces in this video (seo-search-intent / seo-foundation-vs-ads): near-black radial bg, League Gothic display caps, Montserrat labels, gold accent glow. A single abstracted browser/page chassis (rounded card, muted window-chrome dots, generic address pill — NOT a real captured page, no real logos/wordmarks) tells a two-beat before/after story: ranks well but loses the visitor (dead end, wandering cursor, empty CTA slot, muted/dim treatment) versus the same site redesigned with clear multiple CTAs (gold-lit buttons, one decisive cursor landing). Restrained, confident, full-frame alpha-overlay replacement for a talking-head cut-away.

customize.note: Catalog check: the pinned CLI (0.7.68) has no --query flag (only --type/--tag), so ran `catalog --tag=ui` and `catalog --tag=cursor` instead. Hits were generic (simulated-cursor, oversized-cursor, press-ripple, multiplayer-cursors, dynamic-grid, micro-transitions) — none styled to this project's CSS-custom-property brand system, and installing one would bake in its own generic look, same tradeoff this video's own siblings already hit and rejected (seo-foundation-vs-ads: 'the registry's ... blocks bake in their own generic styling and would break the established CSS custom-property system'). Hand-authored instead, directly reusing this video's proven local primitives verbatim: the card chassis (bg2 fill, gold hairline border, radial glow) and cursor-badge + click-ripple pattern from seo-search-intent, the glow-flash landing pulse from seo-foundation-vs-ads, and the crossfade-to-a-second-instance scene transition device (search-bar -> search-bar-2) applied here as browser-frame -> browser-frame-2. No literal browser-chrome/OS/trademark reproduction — window dots and address pill are abstracted, matching the project's established non-literal-mockup convention. Deliberately does NOT reuse icon-cta-buttons' horizontal 3-icon light-up row (that piece's own signature move, built as the very next graphic in this timeline) — CTAs here are bound to distinct page positions (sticky top pill, hero button, floating chat bubble, footer bar) so this piece leads into it without repeating its device.

highlights.label: #1 ranking badge pops onto the browser chassis — the site ranks well
dashed empty slot where a call-to-action should be — nothing to click
cursor drifts aimlessly, never lands, exits the frame — visitor bounces
same chassis flips to the redesigned page — the pivot beat
multiple CTAs stagger onto the page (Get a Quote / Call / Chat / Book Now)
cursor lands decisively on Get a Quote — click-ripple, converts
RANKING GETS THEM THERE. / CTAS GET THEM TO CALL.

scenes.beat: Ranks well, but the visitor hits a dead end and bounces
scenes.description: Abstract browser-page chassis (dark card, gold hairline border, muted window-chrome dots + address pill, no real URL/logo) scale-grows in. A gold '#1' rank badge pops onto its top-right corner — the site ranks. Inside: a placeholder headline bar + subhead bar, and where a call-to-action should sit, only a dim dashed empty outline breathes faintly. A small muted cursor drifts through the page with no clear destination, hovers near the empty slot without landing, then drifts off the right edge and fades — the visitor bounces. A small caption reads 'RANKS. BUT LOSES THEM.'
scenes.motion: bg-fill fade_in 0-0.2s; browser-frame scale_grow (back.out) 0.15-0.55s; rank-badge scale_punch + glow-flash at 0.65s; headline/subhead bars fade_in stagger 0.85-1.15s; empty-cta-slot fade_in 1.3s then a slow breathing opacity pulse (finite repeat) from 1.5s; cursor-wander fade/scale in at 1.6s, drifts through 3 waypoints (sine.inOut, aimless) 1.6-2.9s, hovers near empty-cta-slot ~2.1s without landing, then slides off-frame + fades 3.0-3.4s; dead-end-label fade_in 1.7s; clip ends 3.6s (hard cut to the flip, no manual exit fade — matches this project's established clip-boundary-swap convention)

scenes.beat: Same site, flipped — multiple clear CTAs, and the visitor converts
scenes.description: A second instance of the same chassis (browser-frame-2, identical position/style) pops in at the clip boundary with a snap + glow flash, reading as 'flip, not a new site.' The same headline/subhead bars are present, but the slot that was empty is now a lit gold 'GET A QUOTE' button. Three more CTAs stagger onto the page in their own spots: a sticky 'CALL' pill top-right, a floating circular 'CHAT' bubble bottom-right (echoing the rank-badge's corner from scene 1), and a 'BOOK NOW' bar at the bottom. A bright cursor pops in and lands decisively on Get a Quote — click-ripple, glow-pulse, confirmed. The piece closes on two stacked lines: 'RANKING GETS THEM THERE.' / 'CTAS GET THEM TO CALL.', then holds.
scenes.motion: browser-frame-2 fromTo scale 0.94->1 + opacity, back.out(1.8), at 3.6s (the flip); cta-hero (Get a Quote) pops in with the frame at 3.6s already in its lit gold state (no separate reveal — it reads as 'this is what was missing, now filled'); cta-top/cta-chat/cta-footer scale_punch stagger 0.22s apart from 4.0-4.66s, each with a brief glow-flash landing pulse; cursor-convert pops in at cta-hero (scale 0->1, back.out) at 4.9s, click-ripple + button confirm-bump + glow-intensify at 5.6s; closing-line-1 fade_up at 6.6s, closing-line-2 fade_up+glow at 6.75s; freeze-hold to 7.2s for a clean cut back to host footage
